title: Programmatic Navigation with useRouter
description: Navigate imperatively using the useRouter hook – perfect for form submits, timeouts, and user interactions.

slides.title: Beyond Link: The Router Object 🧭
slides.content:
# `useRouter` Hook

`useRouter` gives you access to the router object, which contains:

* `push(url)` – Navigate to a new page, adding a history entry.
* `replace(url)` – Navigate but replace the current history entry.
* `back()` – Go back one step in history.
* `pathname`, `query`, `asPath` – Information about the current route.

Import from `next/router`.

slides.title: Using push() on Button Click (pages/contact.js)
slides.content: Navigate after form submission or any user action.

quizData.question: What is the difference between `router.push` and `router.replace`?

options.text: `replace` adds a new history entry, `push` doesn't
`push` adds a new history entry, `replace` overwrites the current one

quizData.explanation: `push` lets the user go back to the previous page. `replace` eliminates the current page from history, useful after login to prevent going back to the login page.

slides.title: Go Back Button (pages/404.js example)
slides.content: `router.back()` acts like the browser's back button.

quizData.question: Where can you use the `useRouter` hook?

options.text: In any React component inside the Next.js app

quizData.explanation: `useRouter` is a React hook and can be used in any component, as long as it's inside the Next.js application context.

slides.title: Don't Overuse Programmatic Navigation ⚠️
slides.content: Prefer declarative `<Link>` components when possible. Use `useRouter` only for side‑effect navigation like after submitting a form, or when you need conditional logic that can't be expressed with a link.
